title.title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
title.subtitle: Claim: weak globular $\infty$-groupoids have the homotopy theory of spaces, as Grothendieck guessed

plain: Grothendieck guessed that shapes, up to stretching, are the same as a purely algebraic gadget; this proves it

lines.tex: X \hookrightarrow X^{+} \ \text{ is a weak equivalence}

beats.text: Schematically, at $n = 1$: old cell $f$; adjoin a parallel $g$ and a cell $\theta$ from $f$ to $g$
Henry reduced the hypothesis to one step: this expansion changes no homotopy
The paper proves that step for every coherator in the Ara–Henry convention

steps: Henry: one step is enough. Adding a cell and a witness changes nothing
The paper tracks every composite this creates, using tree-shaped data
So the step holds, and with it Grothendieck's hypothesis

achievement.label: Grothendieck's homotopy hypothesis (Pursuing Stacks, 1983)
achievement.context: Via Henry's pushout conjecture (2018); strict $\infty$-groupoids provably fail
achievement.note: For coherators in the Ara–Henry convention, not every model

verify.detail: Lean: the elementary-expansion theorem, about 12,800 lines; not the model structure or comparison
verify.ourCheck: We read the Comparator statement; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Add a cell and a witness linking it to an old one. Nothing should change.
Every composite this creates is tracked using tree shaped data, so nothing changes.

sources.quote: Henry (2018) isolated the pushout conjecture (his Conj. 5.3.3)
Key step: Henry's pushout conjecture, that elementary expansions X -> X+ (adjoin a parallel n-cell and an (n+1)-cell) are weak equivalences.
The pushout theorem itself is in Lean (`OAI.Grothendieck.elementary_expansion`, about 12,800 lines); the semi-model structure and the comparison with spaces are not.

I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed), so 'formalized' means the release ships a sorry-free, axiom-free (propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice only) proof whose Comparator statement I read.
